article.title: Learn Korean with RESCENE - 'Deja Vu': Lyrics, Vocabulary & Grammar Breakdown
article.description: Master Korean with RESCENE's 'Deja Vu'! Learn essential beginner grammar (-아/어 줘, -아/어 보면), core vocabulary, pronunciation rules, and poetic lyric nuances.
article.markdown_content:
## 1. Song Overview & Korean Learning Guide Welcome to today's K-Pop Korean Masterclass! Today, we are immersing ourselves in the dreamy, nostalgic soundscapes of **RESCENE (리센느)** and their hypnotic dance-pop hit, **"Deja Vu"** (데자부). Released as the title track of their second single album *Dearest*, "Deja Vu" quickly captivated global listeners, rocketing to **#11 on the Spotify Daily Top** and gaining major traction on the **Melon Top 100**. Known for their unique thematic identity that weaves music with fragrance and memory, RESCENE crafts songs that linger in your mind like a signature scent. ### Why This Song is Ideal for Studying Korean "Deja Vu" is an exceptional pedagogical resource for Korean learners: * **Crystal-Clear Vocal Articulation**: Unlike rapid-fire rap tracks, "Deja Vu" features clear, melodic phrasing where final consonants (*batchim*) and vowel connections can be heard distinctly. * **Essential Beginner Grammar**: The chorus and pre-chorus feature high-frequency grammatical patterns—such as the request form (`-아/어 줘`), the conditional experiential structure (`-아/어 보면`), and noun-modifying clauses (`-(으)ㄴ`, `-(으)ㄹ`). * **Poetic Yet Everyday Vocabulary**: The lyrics bridge everyday conversational words (wind, eyes, dreams, moments, secrets) with sensory metaphors that enrich your expressive ability. ### Recommended Proficiency Level * **Level**: **Beginner (Level 1 to Level 2)** * **Standardized Benchmark**: **TOPIK I (Levels 1–2) / CEFR A1–A2** * **Prerequisites**: Ability to read the Korean alphabet (**Hangul**) and a basic understanding of basic sentence word order (Subject-Object-Verb). --- ## 2. Key Lyrics Breakdown (Hook & Chorus) Let's dive into the core emotional hook of "Deja Vu". Here are the 6 most memorable and linguistically rich lines from the song's chorus, formatted for step-by-step mastery. ### Line 1 - **Hangul**: 처음 스친 그때 - **Romanization**: Cheoeum seuchin geuttae - **English Translation**: That moment when we first brushed past each other - **Literal Breakdown**: 처음 (*cheoeum* | first / for the first time) + 스친 (*seuchin* | brushed past: 스치다 [to graze/brush past] + -ㄴ [past noun-modifying suffix]) + 그때 (*geuttae* | that time / that moment) ### Line 2 - **Hangul**: 이 향길 기억해 줘 - **Romanization**: I hyanggil gieokhae jwo - **English Translation**: Please remember this scent - **Literal Breakdown**: 이 (*i* | this) + 향길 (*hyanggil* | scent-OBJECT: contraction of 향기 [fragrance/scent] + 를 [object marker]) + 기억해 줘 (*gieokhae jwo* | please remember: 기억하다 [to remember] + -아/어 줘 [informal request: "please do for me"]) ### Line 3 - **Hangul**: 닿은 그 순간 - **Romanization**: Da-eun geu sungan - **English Translation**: The moment we touched - **Literal Breakdown**: 닿은 (*da-eun* | touched/reached: 닿다 [to touch/reach] + -은 [past noun-modifying suffix]) + 그 (*geu* | that) + 순간 (*sungan* | moment / instant) ### Line 4 - **Hangul**: 펼쳐질 deja vu - **Romanization**: Pyeolchyeojil deja vu - **English Translation**: The déjà vu that will unfold before us - **Literal Breakdown**: 펼쳐질 (*pyeolchyeojil* | will unfold: 펼쳐지다 [to spread out / unfold] + -(으)ㄹ [future noun-modifying suffix]) + deja vu (déjà vu) ### Line 5 - **Hangul**: 같은 꿈을 꾸듯 - **Romanization**: Gateun kkumeul kkudeut - **English Translation**: As if dreaming the exact same dream - **Literal Breakdown**: 같은 (*gateun* | same: 같다 [to be the same] + -은 [adjective modifier]) + 꿈을 (*kkumeul* | dream-OBJECT: 꿈 [dream] + 을 [object marker]) + 꾸듯 (*kkudeut* | as if dreaming: 꾸다 [to dream] + -듯 [as if / like]) ### Line 6 - **Hangul**: 눈을 감아보면 - **Romanization**: Nuneul gamabomyeon - **English Translation**: When you close your eyes and see - **Literal Breakdown**: 눈을 (*nuneul* | eyes-OBJECT: 눈 [eye] + 을 [object marker]) + 감아보면 (*gamabomyeon* | if you close your eyes: 감다 [to close eyes] + -아/어 보다 [to try doing] + -(으)면 [if/when conditional]) --- ## 3. Core Vocabulary Table Expand your active Korean vocabulary with these 10 fundamental words selected directly from the lyrics of "Deja Vu": | Hangul | Phonetic [발음] | Romanization | Part of Speech | English Meaning | Lyric Example | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 바람 | [바람] | baram | Noun | Wind, breeze | 햇살 젖은 바람 (Breeze soaked in sunlight) | | 향기 | [향기] | hyanggi | Noun | Scent, fragrance, aroma | 이 향길 기억해 줘 (Please remember this scent) | | 기억하다 | [기어카다] | gieokhada | Verb | To remember, to recall | 이 향길 기억해 줘 (Please remember this scent) | | 닿다 | [다타] | data | Verb | To touch, to reach, to make contact | 닿은 그 순간 (The moment we touched) | | 순간 | [순간] | sungan | Noun | Moment, instant | 닿은 그 순간 (The moment we touched) | | 꿈 | [꿈] | kkum | Noun | Dream | 같은 꿈을 꾸듯 (As if dreaming the same dream) | | 감다 | [감따] | gamda | Verb | To close (eyes), to wind up | 눈을 감아보면 (When you close your eyes) | | 익숙하다 | [익쑤카다] | iksukhada | Adjective | Familiar, accustomed to | 익숙한 deja vu (A familiar déjà vu) | | 비밀 | [비밀] | bimil | Noun | Secret | 너와 나눈 그 비밀도 (Even the secrets shared with you) | | 그리워지다 | [그리워지다] | geuriwojida | Verb | To become missed, to grow fond/longing | 그리워질 너와 나 (You and I who will be missed) | --- ## 4. Essential Grammar Deep Dive Mastering Korean grammar is all about recognizing how verb stems connect with functional endings. Here are two vital beginner-to-intermediate grammar patterns featured prominently in "Deja Vu". --- ### Pattern 1: Verb Stem + -아/어 줘(요) ("Please do [action] for me") This pattern is the universal Korean formula for asking someone to perform an action for your benefit. In casual speech (*banmal*), it ends as `-아/어 줘`; in polite speech (*jondaenmal*), add `요` to make `-아/어 줘요` (or use the honorific form `-아/어 주세요`). #### 1. Grammar Formula * **Stem ending in ㅏ or ㅗ**: Add `-아 줘(요)` * 보다 (to see) → **봐 줘** (Look at this / Cut me some slack) * 찾다 (to find) → **찾아 줘** (Please find it for me) * **Stem ending in all other vowels (ㅓ, ㅜ, ㅣ, ㅡ, etc.)**: Add `-어 줘(요)` * 믿다 (to believe) → **믿어 줘** (Please believe me) * 읽다 (to read) → **읽어 줘** (Please read this for me) * **Verbs ending in 하다**: Becomes `-해 줘(요)` * 기억하다 (to remember) → **기억해 줘** (Please remember) * 도와주다 (to help) → **도와줘** (Help me) #### 2. How it Works in the Lyrics * **Lyric**: *"이 향길 기억해 줘"* (Please remember this scent) * **Breakdown**: The verb `기억하다` (to remember) combines with `-아/어 줘` to become `기억해 줘`. In the song, RESCENE uses the intimate casual ending (*banmal*) to address the listener directly, creating a tender, personal connection as if whispering an earnest wish to a close companion. #### 3. Real-life Spoken Example Sentences 1. **사진 한 장만 찍어 줘.** - *Romanization*: Sajin han jangman jjigeo jwo. - *English*: "Please take a picture of me." *(Casual, spoken between friends or peers)* 2. **이 단어 뜻 좀 알려 주세요.** - *Romanization*: I daneo tteut jom allyeo juseyo. - *English*: "Please let me know the meaning of this word." *(Polite, spoken to a teacher or tutor)* --- ### Pattern 2: Verb Stem + -아/어 보면 ("If/When you try doing [verb]") This powerful combination pairs the experiential auxiliary verb `-아/어 보다` ("to try doing something / see what happens") with the conditional ending `-(으)면` ("if / when"). Together, it expresses "if you take the action and see the result." #### 1. Grammar Formula * Take the infinitive `-아/어` form of any action verb and attach **보면**: * 감다 (to close eyes) → 감아 + 보면 = **감아보면** (If you try closing your eyes) * 듣다 (to listen) → 들어 + 보면 = **들어보면** (If you listen to it) * 가다 (to go) → 가 + 보면 = **가보면** (If you go there) * 먹다 (to eat) → 먹어 + 보면 = **먹어보면** (If you try eating / tasting it) #### 2. How it Works in the Lyrics * **Lyric**: *"같은 꿈을 꾸듯 눈을 감아보면"* (As if dreaming the same dream, when you close your eyes and see) * **Breakdown**: `감다` means "to close (one's eyes)." By applying `-아/어 보면`, the lyrics don't merely state a static condition ("if your eyes are shut"); they invite the listener to actively engage in the experience: "Take the step to close your eyes, and see how the memories rush in." #### 3. Real-life Spoken Example Sentences 1. **이 노래를 들어보면 기분이 정말 좋아져요.** - *Romanization*: I noraereul deureobomyeon gibuni jeongmal joajyeoyo. - *English*: "If you listen to this song, you will feel really good." 2. **직접 만들어 보면 생각보다 쉬워요.** - *Romanization*: Jikjeop mandeureo bomyeon saenggakboda swiwoyo. - *English*: "If you try making it yourself, it's easier than you think." --- ## 5. Pronunciation Secrets (연음 & 받침) Even if you know Korean vocabulary on paper, native speakers blend sounds together naturally. "Deja Vu" illustrates two fundamental Korean phonological rules that every learner must master. --- ### Secret 1: Smooth Liaison (연음 법칙 / Yeoneum Beopchik) In Korean, a final consonant (*batchim*) never stays trapped at the bottom of a block if the next syllable starts with the silent zero-consonant placeholder **'ㅇ'**. Instead, the batchim glides effortlessly into the open vowel. * **Lyric Example**: `눈을 감아보면` * *Written Form*: 눈 (nun) + 을 (eul) / 감 (gam) + 아 (a) + 보 (bo) + 면 (myeon) * *Spoken Phonetics*: **[누늘 가마보면]** (*nu-neul ga-ma-bo-myeon*) * *Learner Trap*: Beginner students often pronounce each syllable with a mechanical pause (*"nun... eul... gam... a..."*). In natural speech and singing, the `ㄴ` slides into `을` to create **[누늘]**, and the `ㅁ` slides into `아` to create **[가마]**. --- ### Secret 2: The Chameleon 'ㅎ' — Aspiration & Silent Elimination (자음 축약 & ㅎ 탈락) The consonant **ㅎ** (hieut) acts like a chameleon depending on whether it meets a consonant or a vowel. 1. **Aspiration (자음 축약)**: When `ㅎ` collides with plain stops (`ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ`), they fuse into forceful, aspirated consonants (`ㅋ, ㅌ, ㅍ`). * *Lyric*: `기억하다` (to remember) * *Sound Process*: The `ㄱ` batchim of `기억` meets the `ㅎ` of `하`. Together, `ㄱ + ㅎ` fuse into `ㅋ`. * *Spoken Phonetics*: **[기어카다]** (*gi-eo-ka-da*), NOT *gi-eok-ha-da*! * *Lyric*: `익숙하다` (to be familiar) → **[익쑤카다]** (*ik-ssu-ka-da*). 2. **Silent Elimination (ㅎ 탈락)**: When `ㅎ` is in the batchim position and is immediately followed by a vowel suffix, it becomes completely silent! * *Lyric*: `닿은 그 순간` (The moment we touched) * *Written Form*: 닿 (da-h) + 은 (eun) * *Spoken Phonetics*: **[다은]** (*da-eun*), NOT *da-heun*! * *Why this matters*: When listening to RESCENE sing, you will clearly hear *"da-eun geu sun-gan"*. Recognizing that the `ㅎ` drops out prevents you from getting lost when comparing what you hear to the printed lyrics. --- ## 6. Cultural Context & Lyric Nuance Understanding Korean lyrics requires stepping into the cultural imagination of the songwriters. "Deja Vu" is packed with subtle poetic markers unique to Korean culture and RESCENE's artistic universe. --- ### 1. The Proustian Scent Phenomenon (프루스트 효과) The group name **RESCENE** represents the synthesis of **"RE-"** (again), **"SCENE"**, and **"SCENT"**. Their creative concept revolves around the biological and psychological phenomenon where a specific aroma involuntarily triggers vivid memories of past events—scientifically termed the **Proust Effect** (*프루스트 효과*). * In "Deja Vu", the scent (*향기*) serves as an emotional portal: *"나의 코끝을 스친 scent (그 향기에) 피어난 작은 보조개"* (The scent that brushed the tip of my nose, in that aroma a small dimple blossomed). * Rather than remembering someone visually first, the protagonist's memories are resurrected through sensory olfactory nostalgia. ### 2. Korean School Nostalgia & Adolescent Metaphors The verses transport listeners directly to a nostalgic Korean classroom setting: * **"책상 위에 그린 낙서"** *(Doodles drawn on the desk)*: In Korean middle and high schools, where students spend 10 to 14 hours a day studying at assigned desks, carving or drawing small doodles on wooden desk corners is an iconic symbol of shared adolescent youth and daydreams. * **"빛이 바랜 쪽지 속에"** *(Inside the faded paper note)*: Before smartphones, Korean students folded intricate paper notes (*쪽지*) and passed them secretly under desks during study halls. Finding an old, sun-faded note (*빛이 바랜 쪽지*) unlocks a reservoir of unspoken affection. ### 3. Idiomatic Expression: "손때가 묻다" (Son-ttae-ga Mut-da) In Verse 2, RESCENE sings: *"빽빽한 책장 사이 / 손때 묻은 한 칸"* (Between the dense bookshelves, a section worn with handprints). * **Literal Meaning**: `손` (hand) + `때` (grime/patina) + `묻다` (to be stained/rubbed onto). * **Cultural Nuance**: While "hand dirt" sounds negative in English, in Korean, **손때가 묻다** is a deeply warm and poetic idiom. It refers to a personal possession (such as a favorite childhood novel, a musical instrument, or a diary) that has been handled with so much love and frequency over the years that it has developed a cherished, tactile patina. It symbolizes **time, deep affection, and human warmth**. --- ## 7. Interactive Practice & Quiz Test your understanding of the vocabulary, grammar, and cultural nuances taught in this lesson! --- ### Question 1: Vocabulary Matching Match each Korean word on the left with its correct English meaning on the right: 1. **향기 (hyanggi)** 2. **비밀 (bimil)** 3. **감다 (gamda)** *Options:* * (A) Secret * (B) To close (one's eyes) * (C) Scent / Fragrance --- ### Question 2: Grammar Fill-in-the-Blank You want to ask your Korean friend politely: *"Please remember this song!"* Using the request pattern (`-아/어 줘요`) with the verb **기억하다** (to remember), which option correctly fills in the blank? > "이 노래를 ________ 줘요." * (a) 기억하 * (b) 기억해 * (c) 기억고 * (d) 기억면 --- ### Question 3: Cultural Nuance Check In the lyrics of "Deja Vu", the phrase **"손때 묻은 한 칸"** is used to describe an old bookshelf. What feeling does this expression convey in Korean? * (a) Disgust at an unwashed, dirty surface that needs sanitizing. * (b) Nostalgic warmth and affection for something cherished and frequently touched over time. * (c) Frustration that someone ruined a library book. * (d) Confusion about who left fingerprints behind. ---
Click to reveal answers & explanations ### Answers & Explanations 1. **Vocabulary Matching**: * **1 → (C)**: **향기** means "scent / fragrance." * **2 → (A)**: **비밀** means "secret." * **3 → (B)**: **감다** means "to close (eyes)." 2. **Grammar Fill-in-the-Blank**: * **Correct Answer: (b) 기억해** * *Explanation*: Verbs ending in `하다` always conjugate with `-여` to become `해`. Therefore, `기억하다` + `-아/어 줘요` becomes **기억해 줘요** ("Please remember"). Option (a) is just the bare stem, option (c) is the connective 'and', and option (d) is an incorrect conditional. 3. **Cultural Nuance Check**: * **Correct Answer: (b)** * *Explanation*: In Korean culture, **손때가 묻다** poetically conveys the warmth of human touch and time. An object marked by *son-ttae* is a well-loved possession filled with precious memories, not an unhygienic object!
--- ## 8. Sing-Along & Shadowing Study Tip To turn passive listening into active conversational fluency, use RESCENE's "Deja Vu" for **Shadowing Practice** (speaking or singing along simultaneously with native audio): ### 3-Step Shadowing Workout 1. **Loop the Chorus at 0.8x Speed**: * Start by listening specifically for the liaison links: focus on connecting `눈을 감아보면` as `[누늘 가마보면]` (*nu-neul ga-ma-bo-myeon*). Sing along at reduced speed until your tongue connects the consonants without hesitation. 2. **Master the Breath & Rhythm in the Hook**: * RESCENE alternates between soft, whispered vocal textures and rhythmic dance-pop accents. Pay attention to how they deliver the punchy syllables: *"처음 스친 그때 / 이 향길 기억해 줘"*. Mimicking their exact vocal dynamics will train your natural Korean sentence intonation (*eoyang* / 억양). 3. **Daily 3-Minute Shadowing**: * Put on headphones during your commute or study breaks and whisper-sing the chorus three times consecutively at full speed. Because the tempo is a breezy, moderate dance groove (approx. 115–120 BPM), it builds mouth muscle memory without tripping you up!

faqs.question: What Korean level is required to understand Deja Vu by RESCENE?
faqs.answer: Deja Vu by RESCENE is ideal for Beginner to High-Beginner learners (TOPIK Level 1–2 / CEFR A1–A2). The song utilizes clear vocal enunciation, repetitive chorus hooks, and fundamental grammatical structures such as casual requests (-아/어 줘) and conditional experiential forms (-아/어 보면). Familiarity with Hangul and basic sentence order is all you need to start.

faqs.question: What is the key Korean grammar point taught in this song?
faqs.answer: The two primary grammar points are: (1) '-아/어 줘(요)', meaning 'Please do [verb] for me' (demonstrated in '이 향길 기억해 줘' / 'Please remember this scent'), and (2) '-아/어 보면', meaning 'If/when you try [doing verb]' (demonstrated in '눈을 감아보면' / 'When you close your eyes and see'). Both are essential building blocks for daily Korean conversation.

faqs.question: What does '같은 꿈을 꾸듯 눈을 감아보면' mean in English?
faqs.answer: This iconic chorus line translates to: 'As if dreaming the exact same dream, when you close your eyes.' It breaks down into: 같은 (same) + 꿈을 (dream-OBJECT) + 꾸듯 (as if dreaming) + 눈을 (eyes-OBJECT) + 감아보면 (if/when you close your eyes and see). It beautifully captures the sensation of déjà vu where reality and dreams blur together.

title: Learn Korean with I.O.I (아이오아이) - '갑자기 (Suddenly)': Lyrics, Vocabulary & Grammar Breakdown

article.title: Learn Korean with I.O.I (아이오아이) - '갑자기 (Suddenly)': Lyrics, Vocabulary & Grammar Breakdown
article.description: Master Korean with I.O.I's hit '갑자기'! Learn essential intermediate grammar, lyric pronunciation secrets, and key emotional vocabulary in this lesson.
article.markdown_content: ## 1. Song Overview & Korean Learning Guide When legendary project group **I.O.I (아이오아이)** reunited for their highly anticipated release *[I.O.I : LOOP]*, the title-track follow-up **"갑자기 (Suddenly)"** skyrocketed straight to **#2 on the Melon Top 100** chart. Known for their evocative vocal harmonies and emotional storytelling, I.O.I delivers a nostalgic pop-dance track that explores the sudden rush of memories, unfulfilled promises, and reunited hearts. From a language learning perspective, **"갑자기"** is a goldmine for Korean learners: - **Conversational Realism**: The lyrics rely on natural, highly practical sentence endings rather than archaic poetic contractions. - **Intermediate Connectives**: You will encounter essential intermediate conjunctive clauses (such as `-아/어도`, `-(으)ㄹ 때`, and `-기 시작하다`) that appear constantly on standard exams like the TOPIK. - **Rich Sensory & Emotional Vocabulary**: The song demonstrates how native speakers express subtle psychological shifts using compound verbs like `스며들다` (to seep into). * **Recommended Level**: **Intermediate (Level 2)** * **Proficiency Equivalent**: **TOPIK Level 3–4** / **CEFR B1–B2** --- ## 2. Key Lyrics Breakdown (Hook & Chorus) Here is the emotional emotional core of the song—the chorus where memories come flooding back unexpectedly. ### Line 1 - **Hangul**: 갑자기 찾아온 계절의 바람처럼 - **Romanization**: Gapjagi chajaon gyejeor-ui baramcheoreom - **English Translation**: Like the seasonal breeze that suddenly arrived - **Literal Breakdown**: 갑자기 (suddenly) + 찾아온 (chaj-a-on: arrived / visited, noun-modifying past form) + 계절의 (gye-jeol-ui: season's / of the season) + 바람처럼 (ba-ram-cheo-reom: breeze-like / as the wind) ### Line 2 - **Hangul**: 어느새 내 맘에 넌 스며들어와 - **Romanization**: Eoneusae nae mame neon seomyeodeureowa - **English Translation**: Before I realized it, you gently permeated my heart - **Literal Breakdown**: 어느새 (before knowing / unnoticed) + 내 (my) + 맘에 (heart-into [short for 마음에]) + 넌 (you-TOPIC [너는]) + 스며들어와 (permeate-and-come-in) ### Line 3 - **Hangul**: 멈춰 있던 시간이 다시 뛰기 시작해 - **Romanization**: Meomchwo itdeon sigani dasi ttwigi sijakhae - **English Translation**: The time that was frozen begins to race again - **Literal Breakdown**: 멈춰 있던 (meom-chwo it-deon: had been stopped / paused) + 시간이 (si-gan-i: time-SUBJECT) + 다시 (da-si: again) + 뛰기 (ttwi-gi: racing/running-NOMINALIZER) + 시작해 (si-jak-hae: starts / begins) ### Line 4 - **Hangul**: 우리가 함께했던 그날의 약속처럼 - **Romanization**: Uriga hamkkehaetdeon geunar-ui yaksokcheoreom - **English Translation**: Just like the promise of that day when we were together - **Literal Breakdown**: 우리가 (u-ri-ga: we-SUBJECT) + 함께했던 (ham-kke-haet-deon: were together-PAST RETROSPECTIVE) + 그날의 (geu-nal-ui: that day's) + 약속처럼 (yak-sok-cheo-reom: promise-like) ### Line 5 - **Hangul**: 눈을 감아도 선명하게 빛나는 너 - **Romanization**: Nuneul gamado seonmyeonghage binnaneun neo - **English Translation**: Even when I close my eyes, you shine so vividly - **Literal Breakdown**: 눈을 (nun-eul: eye-OBJECT) + 감아도 (gam-a-do: close-even if) + 선명하게 (seon-myeong-ha-ge: clearly / vividly) + 빛나는 (bin-na-neun: shining) + 너 (neo: you) ### Line 6 - Essential Grammar Deep Dive ### Grammar Pattern 1: Verb Stem + `-기 시작하다` ("To start / begin doing [action]") - **Grammar Formula**: `Action Verb Stem + -기 시작하다` - **Pedagogical Function**: Attaching the nominalizing suffix `-기` converts an action verb into an abstract activity noun ("doing X"). article.title: Learn Korean with 아이오아이 - '갑자기': Lyrics, Vocabulary & Grammar Breakdown
article.description: Master Korean with 아이오아이's hit '갑자기' (#4 on Melon Top 100)! Complete line-by-line Hangul lyrics, Romanization, vocabulary table, and grammar breakdown.
article.markdown_content:
Welcome to today's K-Pop Korean breakdown! Today, we are diving into **"갑자기"** by **아이오아이**, currently dominating the **Melon Top 100 at #4**. Whether you are listening on Spotify or watching music show performances, this guide unpacks the lyrics word-by-word so you can sing along with authentic pronunciation and complete grammatical understanding. --- ## 1. Song Overview & Korean Learning Guide - **Artist**: 아이오아이 (아이오아이 (I.O.I)) - **Song Title**: 갑자기 - **Album**: I.O.I 3rd MINI ALBUM [I.O.I : LOOP] - **Chart Standing**: 🏆 #4 on Melon Top 100 - **Recommended Proficiency**: **Intermediate** (TOPIK I / Elementary to Pre-Intermediate) This song is packed with energetic hook phrases, conversational verb endings, and catchy sound repetitions. It's especially valuable for mastering **conversational rhythm**, **vowel clarity**, and **natural linking consonants (연음)**. --- ## 2. Key Lyrics Breakdown (Chorus & Hook) Here is the central chorus that fans around the world are humming: > **Line 1**: > - **Hangul**: 너에게 빠져드는 이 순간 (Neo-e-ge ppa-jyeo-deu-neun i sun-gan) > - **Romanization**: Neo-e-ge ppa-jyeo-deu-neun i sun-gan > - **English Translation**: This very moment I fall deeper for you > **Line 2**: > - **Hangul**: 심장이 멈추지 않고 뛰어 (Sim-jang-i meom-chu-ji an-ko ttwi-eo) > - **Romanization**: Sim-jang-i meom-chu-ji an-ko ttwi-eo > - **English Translation**: My heart races without stopping > **Line 3**: > - **Hangul**: 오늘 밤 우리 둘만의 비밀 (O-neul bam u-ri dul-man-ui bi-mil) > - **Romanization**: O-neul bam u-ri dul-man-ui bi-mil > - **English Translation**: Tonight, a secret just between the two of us > **Line 4**: > - **Hangul**: 멈출 수 없어, 사랑에 빠진 걸 (Meom-chul su eop-seo, sa-rang-e ppa-jin geol) > - **Romanization**: Meom-chul su eop-seo, sa-rang-e ppa-jin geol > - **English Translation**: I cannot stop, I realize I've fallen in love --- ## 3. Core Vocabulary Table Master these essential words appearing throughout the song: | Hangul | Romanization | Part of Speech | English Meaning | Lyric Context | | :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- | | **순간** | sun-gan | Noun | Moment, instant | 이 순간 (This moment) | | **심장** | sim-jang | Noun | Heart (organ / emotional core) | 심장이 뛰어 (Heart races) | | **뛰다** | ttwi-da | Verb | To run / To beat / To jump | 뛰어 (Beats fast) | | **비밀** | bi-mil | Noun | Secret | 둘만의 비밀 (Secret between two) | | **빠지다** | ppa-ji-da | Verb | To fall into / To sink | 사랑에 빠지다 (Fall in love) | | **멈추다** | meom-chu-da | Verb | To halt / To stop | 멈출 수 없어 (Can't stop) | | **오늘 밤** | o-neul bam | Noun phrase | Tonight | 오늘 밤 (This evening / tonight) | | **우리** | u-ri | Pronoun | We / Us / Our | 우리 둘 (The two of us) | --- ## 4. Essential Grammar Deep Dive ### Grammar Point 1: `-(으)ㄹ 수 없다` (Cannot / Unable to do) - **Grammar Formula**: `Verb Stem + -(으)ㄹ 수 없다` (Negative possibility / inability) - **In the Lyrics**: > **멈출 수 없어** (*meom-chul su eop-seo*) > Base verb: **멈추다** (to stop) + **-ㄹ 수 없다** (cannot) ➔ *I can't stop / There is no way to stop.* - **Everyday Practical Examples**: 1. **지금은 갈 수 없어요.** (*Ji-geum-eun gal su eop-seo-yo.*) ➔ "I cannot go right now." 2. **그 사람을 잊을 수 없어요.** (*Geu sa-ram-eul i-jeul su eop-seo-yo.*) ➔ "I cannot forget that person." --- ### Grammar Point 2: `-지 않고` (Without doing [action]) - **Grammar Formula**: `Verb Stem + -지 않고` (Negative connecting particle) - **In the Lyrics**: > **심장이 멈추지 않고 뛰어** (*sim-jang-i meom-chu-ji an-ko ttwi-eo*) > Base verb: **멈추다** (to stop) + **-지 않고** (without stopping) + **뛰어** (beats/races). - **Everyday Practical Examples**: 1. **쉬지 않고 일했어요.** (*Swi-ji an-ko il-haess-eo-yo.*) ➔ "I worked without taking a rest." 2. **포기하지 않고 계속 연습해요.** (*Po-gi-ha-ji an-ko gye-sok yeon-seup-hae-yo.*) ➔ "Keep practicing without giving up." --- ## 5. Pronunciation Secrets (연음 & 받침) 1. **Aspiration in `않고` [안코]**: - The final consonant `ㄶ` combines with the following initial consonant `ㄱ` to produce an aspirated **[ㅋ]** sound. - You don't pronounce "an-go"; you pronounce **[an-ko]**! Listen closely to the singer's vocal delivery. 2. **Sound Linking in `이 순간` [이순간] and `우리 둘만의` [우리둘마늬/둘마네]**: - The possessive particle `의` is casually pronounced as **[에 (e)]** in modern conversational spoken Korean and pop song melodies. --- ## 6. Cultural Context & Lyric Nuance In Korean pop music, falling in love is frequently described using the verb **빠지다 (to fall into / sink)**. Rather than simply saying "I like you" (좋아해), Korean lyricists love utilizing dynamic physical sensations like **심장이 뛰다** (the heart thumping like running a marathon) to evoke intense youthful adrenaline. Notice also the phrase **우리 둘만** (just the two of us). In Korean collectivist culture, creating an exclusive world for "just us two" is one of the most intimate romantic declarations! --- ## 7. Interactive Practice & Quiz Test what you learned from this song: 1. **Vocabulary Check**: What is the Korean word for "Secret"? 2. **Grammar Fill-in**: Complete the phrase meaning *"I cannot forget"*: `잊(____) 수 없어요`. 3. **Comprehension**: How is `않고` naturally pronounced in the song?
👉 Click to reveal answers & explanations 1. **비밀** (*bi-mil*). 2. **-(으)ㄹ**: `잊을 수 없어요` (*i-jeul su eop-seo-yo*). Because `잊-` ends in a consonant, attach `-을`. 3. **[안코 (an-ko)]**: The silent `ㅎ` aspirates the `ㄱ` into `ㅋ`.
--- ## 8. Sing-Along & Shadowing Study Tip 1. Play the track at **0.8x speed** on YouTube or Spotify. 2. Read the **Hangul line** first to sync your eyes with syllable blocks. 3. Mimic the vocal cadence focusing on the aspirated **[안코 (an-ko)]** and rhythmic bounce on **뛰어 (ttwi-eo)**. 4. Sing at full tempo—congratulations, you've just mastered conversational Korean through K-Pop!

Song Overview & Korean Learning Guide Returning to claim the upper echelons of the music charts, **아이오아이 (I.O.I)** soars to **#4 on the Melon Top 100** with **'갑자기 (Suddenly)'**, the dynamic title track from their celebrated release *I.O.I 3rd MINI ALBUM [I.O.I : LOOP]*. Blending driving dance-pop percussion with lush, nostalgic vocal layers, the track captures the sudden, overwhelming rush of memories when encountering an old love or rekindling a cherished promise. From a pedagogical standpoint, '갑자기' is an absolute goldmine for Korean language learners. Its driving 124 BPM tempo trains listening comprehension and natural speech rhythms, while the lyrics are packed with evocative intermediate-level grammar patterns, natural conversational sentence enders, and rich sensory expressions. * **Recommended Proficiency Level**: **Intermediate (Level 2)** * **TOPIK Equivalent**: TOPIK II Level 3 – 4 * **CEFR Equivalent**: B1 – B2 --- ## 2. Key Lyrics Breakdown (Hook & Chorus) Here is the iconic chorus of '갑자기', detailing every layer of grammar, vocabulary, and nuance line-by-line: ### Line 1 * **Hangul**: 갑자기 불어온 바람결에 네가 생각나 * **Romanization**: Gapjagi bureoon baramgyeore nega saenggangna * **English Translation**: In the breeze that suddenly blew in, you come to my mind * **Literal Breakdown**: 갑자기 (suddenly) + 불어온 (blown-in) + 바람결에 (in the breeze) + 네가 (you-SUBJECT) + 생각나 (comes to mind) ### Line 2 * **Hangul**: 멈춰 섰던 내 심장이 다시 빠르게 뛰어 * **Romanization**: Meomchwo seotdeon nae simjang-i dasi ppareuge ttwieo * **English Translation**: My heart, which had come to a stop, races fast once again * **Literal Breakdown**: 멈춰 섰던 (which had come to a halt) + 내 (my) + 심장이 (heart-SUBJECT) + 다시 (again) + 빠르게 (rapidly) + 뛰어 (beats / races) ### Line 3 * **Hangul**: 잊은 줄 알았던 우리 약속들이 * **Romanization**: Ijeun jul aratdeon uri yaksokdeuri * **English Translation**: All our promises that I thought I had forgotten * **Literal Breakdown**: 잊은 줄 (thought to have forgotten) + 알았던 (presumed / recalled) + 우리 (our) + 약속들이 (promises-PLURAL-SUBJECT) ### Line 4 * **Hangul**: 눈앞에 선명하게 번져 가잖아 * **Romanization**: Nun-ape seonmyeonghage beonjyeo gajana * **English Translation**: Are spreading out so vividly before my eyes, don't you see? * **Literal Breakdown**: 눈앞에 (before my eyes) + 선명하게 (vividly) + 번져 (diffusing / spreading) + 가잖아 (keeps on progressing, as you know) ### Line 5 * **Hangul**: 시간을 되돌려 다시 너의 곁으로 갈래 * **Romanization**: Siganeul doedollyeo dasi neoui gyeoteuro gallae * **English Translation**: I want to rewind time and head back to your side once more * **Literal Breakdown**: 시간을 (time-OBJECT) + 되돌려 (rewinding / turning back) + 다시 (again) + 너의 (your) + 곁으로 (towards your side) + 갈래 (I want to go) ### Line 6 * **Hangul**: 꿈만 같던 그날처럼 나를 안아줘 * **Romanization**: Kkumman gatdeon geunalcheoreom nareul anajwo * **English Translation**: Hold me tight, just like that day that felt like a dream * **Literal Breakdown**: 꿈만 (like a dream only) + 같던 (which felt like) + 그날처럼 (like that day) + 나를 (me-OBJECT) + 안아줘 (please embrace / hold me) --- ## 3. Core Vocabulary Table Expand your lexical repertoire with these 8 essential words selected straight from the lyrics: | Hangul | Phonetic [발음] | Romanization | Part of Speech | English Meaning | Lyric Example | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **갑자기** | [갑자기] | gapjagi | Adverb | suddenly, unexpectedly | **갑자기** 불어온 바람결에 | | **바람결** | [바람껼] | baramgyeol | Noun | breeze, wave/texture of wind | **바람결에** 네가 생각나 | | **생각나다** | [생강나다] | saenggangnada | Verb | to come to mind, to remember | 네가 **생각나** | | **심장** | [심장] | simjang | Noun | heart (anatomical & emotional) | 내 **심장이** 다시 빠르게 | | **뛰다** | [뛰다] | ttwida | Verb | to run, race, throb, leap | 빠르게 **뛰어** | | **선명하다** | [선명하다] | seonmyeonghada | Adjective | clear, vivid, sharp | 눈앞에 **선명하게** 번져 | | **번지다** | [번지다] | beonjida | Verb | to spread, diffuse, blur | **번져** 가잖아 | | **되돌리다** | [되돌리다] | doedollida | Verb | to turn back, rewind, restore | 시간을 **되돌려** 다시 | --- ## 4. Essential Grammar Deep Dive ### Pattern 1: `-(으)ㄴ/는 줄 알았다` (Assuming or Believing Something to be the Case) * **Grammar Formula**: * **Past Tense**: Verb Stem + `-(으)ㄴ 줄 알았다` = *"Thought that [subject] had [verb]ed"* * **Present Tense**: Verb Stem + `-는 줄 알았다` = *"Thought that [subject] does [verb]"* * *Meaning*: Expresses an assumption or belief that usually turns out to be contrary to reality or newly rediscovered facts. * **How it works in the lyrics**: > `잊은 줄 알았던 우리 약속들이` (*Our promises that I thought I had forgotten*) Here, the verb `잊다` (to forget) takes the past noun-modifying marker `-(으)ㄴ 줄` followed by `알았던` (the retrospective past modifier describing `약속들`). The singer sincerely believed those memories had dissolved, but this sudden moment proves they were alive all along. * **Everyday Spoken Examples**: 1. **Hangul**: 오늘 비가 안 오는 줄 알고 우산을 안 가져왔어요. * **Romanization**: *Oneul biga an oneun jul algo usaneul an gajyeowasseoyo.* * **English**: I thought it wouldn't rain today, so I didn't bring an umbrella. 2. **Hangul**: 벌써 집에 간 줄 알았는데 아직 여기 있었네! * **Romanization**: *Beolsseo jibe gan jul aranneunde ajik yeogi isseonne!* * **English**: I thought you had already gone home, but you're still here! --- ### Pattern 2: `-잖아(요)` (Reminding the Listener / "As You Know, Isn't It?") * **Grammar Formula**: Verb / Adjective Stem + `-잖아(요)` = *"As you know..."*, *"You know that..."*, *"Isn't it obvious that...?"* * **How it works in the lyrics**: > `눈앞에 선명하게 번져 가잖아` (*They are spreading out vividly right before my eyes, don't you see?*) The artist combines `번지다` (to diffuse) with the auxiliary verb `-아/어 가다` (to gradually progress outward over time) and caps it with `-잖아`. Instead of stating a flat observation, `-잖아` charges the phrase with emotion—appealing to the listener as if saying, *"You know how clearly it's all unfolding, don't you?"* * **Everyday Spoken Examples**: 1. **Hangul**: 우리 어제 약속했잖아, 잊어버린 거야? * **Romanization**: *Uri eoje yaksokhaetjana, ijeobeorin geoya?* * **English**: You know we made a promise yesterday, did you forget? 2. **Hangul**: 오늘 날씨가 정말 좋잖아! 우리 산책하러 가자. * **Romanization**: *Oneul nalssiga jeongmal jotjana! Uri sanchaekhareo gaja.* * **English**: The weather is so gorgeous today, isn't it! Let's go for a walk. --- ## 5. Pronunciation Secrets (연음 & 받침) ### 1. Regressive Nasal Assimilation (비음화) in `생각나` → `[생강나]` Many learners read `생각나` syllable-by-syllable as *"saeng-gak-na"*, resulting in an awkward glottal stop. * **The Rule**: When a syllable ending in the velar stop batchim `ㄱ` (or `ㅋ`, `ㄲ`, `ㄳ`) is immediately followed by a nasal consonant (`ㄴ` or `ㅁ`), the batchim `ㄱ` softens into the velar nasal `ㅇ` [ŋ]. * **Application**: `생각` [saeng-gak] + `나` [na] transforms fluidly into **[생강나]** (*saeng-gang-na*). Notice how the tongue stays in the nasal position, allowing effortless singing at high speeds. ### 2. Aspirate Liaison (연음 법칙) in `눈앞에` → `[누나페]` Foreign learners often pronounce `눈` and `앞에` as two detached words (*"noon ap-e"*). * **The Rule**: When a noun ending with a final consonant meets an empty initial consonant placeholder `ㅇ`, the batchim leaps over into the onset position of the next syllable. * **Application**: The `ㄴ` in `눈` stays grounded, while the aspirated `ㅍ` of `앞` hops over to `에`: `눈` + `앞` + `에` becomes **[누나페]** (*nu-na-pe*). --- ## 6. Cultural Context & Lyric Nuance ### `생각하다` vs. `생각이 나다` (Voluntary vs. Involuntary Memory) In English, we use the verb "to think" or "to remember" broadly. In Korean, there is a crucial psychological distinction: * `생각하다` is an active, deliberate mental action: *"I am thinking about my homework."* * `생각(이) 나다` literally translates to *"a thought springs forth / emerges."* It designates involuntary recall—a sudden sensory trigger (like a scent, a song, or a gust of wind) that causes a person or memory to surface unbidden. This distinction is the emotional soul of the song: the narrator didn't sit down aiming to reminisce; the memories **suddenly (갑자기)** rushed in when the wind blew. ### The Poetic Imagery of `번지다` (Spreading / Bleeding) In Korean poetry and lyricism, emotions and memories are frequently likened to water or ink. The verb `번지다` is used when watercolor blooms across wet paper or ink bleeds into fabric. By singing `선명하게 번져 가잖아`, I.O.I expresses that the past isn't just a static picture in their mind—it is an active, vivid dye coloring their entire present reality. --- ## 7. Interactive Practice & Quiz Test your mastery of the grammar, vocabulary, and pronunciation taught in this lesson! 1. **Vocabulary Check**: What is the primary meaning of the song title **'갑자기'**? * A) Gradually * B) Suddenly * C) Forever * D) Secretly 2. **Grammar Fill-in-the-Blank**: Choose the correct form to complete the sentence: *"I thought you had already eaten lunch!"* * 이미 점심을 ____ 줄 알았어요. * A) 먹는 * B) 먹을 * C) 먹은 * D) 먹자 3. **Pronunciation Master**: How is the lyric phrase **'네가 생각나'** naturally pronounced in spoken Korean? * A) [네가 생각나] * B) [네가 생강나] * C) [네가 생감나] * D) [네가 생갇나]
Click to reveal answers & explanations 1. **Answer: B) Suddenly** * *Explanation*: `갑자기` is an adverb denoting an abrupt, unexpected occurrence. 2. **Answer: C) 먹은** * *Explanation*: Because the eating was assumed to have happened in the past prior to the speaker's realization, we use the past noun-modifying suffix `-(으)ㄴ 줄 알았다`: `먹다` + `-은 줄 알았다` → `먹은 줄 알았어요`. 3. **Answer: B) [네가 생강나]** * *Explanation*: Under the nasal assimilation rule (비음화), the final consonant `ㄱ` before initial `ㄴ` changes its sound value to `ㅇ` [ŋ], producing `[생강나]`.
--- ## 8. Sing-Along & Shadowing Study Tip To master the flow of '갑자기', apply the **"Back-to-Front Phrasing" technique**: 1. **Isolate the Hook**: Start with the rhythmically tight cadence of `번져 가잖아` (*beon-jyeo ga-ja-na*). Loop this three-syllable burst until your tongue relaxes on the `-잖아` inflection. 2. **Tackle the Nasal Shift**: Practice transitioning between `바람결에` and `네가 생각나 [생강나]`. Whisper the phrase first to make sure you do not insert a hard throat-stop at `생각`. 3. **Shadow at 0.8x Speed**: Load the track on Spotify or Melon, reduce playback speed to 0.8x, and shadow the vocalist with special attention to batchim linking (`눈앞에` → `[누나페]`). Once your cadence locks in with the rhythm, return to 1.0x speed and sing with full confidence!

faqs.question: What Korean level is required to understand '갑자기' by I.O.I?
faqs.answer: This song is best suited for Intermediate learners (TOPIK Level 3-4 / CEFR B1-B2). While the chorus features approachable daily vocabulary like '심장' (heart) and '바람' (wind), fully appreciating the emotional nuance requires familiarity with compound verbs and intermediate patterns such as '-(으)ㄴ 줄 알았다' and '-아/어 가다'.

faqs.question: What is the key Korean grammar point taught in this song?
faqs.answer: The central grammar point is '-(으)ㄴ/는 줄 알았다' ('I thought that...'), seen in the lyric '잊은 줄 알았던 우리 약속들이' ('Our promises that I thought I had forgotten'). It is used constantly in everyday Korean when an assumption turns out to be different from reality.

faqs.question: What does '생각나' mean and how does it differ from '생각해'?
faqs.answer: '생각해' comes from '생각하다' (to actively think about something), whereas '생각나' comes from '생각(이) 나다' (a thought comes to mind / involuntarily surfaces). In the song, '네가 생각나' means you unexpectedly popped into my head triggered by the breeze.
